title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 75-77 of the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes). There is a set or category M of 'pieces' X, each realised in an ambient space P. Each piece has a closed realisation |X| and an open part |X|°, and |X| is the union of the |Y|° over the Y in its closure tilde-X. There is a combinatorial incidence relation Z |o| X: 'disjoint' or 'meeting', read on the open parts. Through it, Grothendieck defines two operators on subsets L of M. The co-support cosupp°(L) is the set of pieces disjoint from L, an orthogonal L^perp. The support supp°(L) is the set of Y such that no Z disjoint from L meets Y, essentially the double orthogonal L^{perp perp}. This is a Birkhoff polarity / Galois-connection closure. Σ_M denotes the closed elements, the 'supports'. The map φ sends a set of pieces to the union of their open parts. The aim is to rebuild 'topological' notions (closures, complements, supports) purely combinatorially from M plus the incidence relation, and to compare them with the geometric realisation. This is part of his programme of a 'tame' analysis situs.

On p.75 he had shown φ(supp°X) = |X|° and φ(cosupp°X) = P \ |X|°. He was proving φ(supp X) = |X| with supp X := supp°(tilde-X). The page opens by saying the reverse inclusion needs the hypothesis stated earlier 'in all its force'. A starred margin note adds that it is needed for finite powers/families, with conditions like |Z| ∩ |X| = ∅ and |Z| ⊂ p^{-1}(|X|); it is largely illegible.

He then doubts the framework is right yet and tests it on a case. Take Y < X (Y a face/specialisation of X) and consider supp°({Y,X}). Clearly |X|° ∪ |Y|° ⊂ φ(supp°{Y,X}). Is the converse true? 'Mais oui.' He now sees the general hypothesis that guarantees good behaviour of '(internal) constructible supports'.

Definition: let F be a notion of 'figures' attached to M. An element A of Σ_M is a constructible (internal) support if A = supp°(L) for some L ⊂ M majorised in F, i.e. L ⊂ F for some figure F ∈ F.

Definition begun at the bottom: an external support functor X ↦ |X|, M → (subsets of P), is 'fully faithful' for F if a property holds. The next page states it: for every F ∈ F, φ(cosupp°F) = P \ |F|. Equivalently, every point outside |F| lies in the open part of some piece Z with |Z|° ⊂ P \ |F|. In words, the complement of a figure is exhausted by open pieces combinatorially disjoint from it.

On p.77 he deduces the proposition φ(supp°(L)) = |L|° := ∪_{X∈L} |X|° for L ⊂ F. This says combinatorial and geometric supports agree on constructible supports. The example on this page, L = {Y,X}, is the test case motivating that hypothesis.
errors: No outright error on this page; it is a test case plus definitions.
The claim that φ(supp°{Y,X}) equals |X|° ∪ |Y|° is asserted ('Mais oui') without proof here. It only follows on p.77 once the full-faithfulness hypothesis is imposed, and fails without it.

There is a notational slip/ambiguity across pages: the same symbol |o| is used both for 'disjoint' and for 'meets' (p.77: Z|o|L meaning disjoint, Z|o|Y meaning meeting). The intended relation must be fixed for the polarity to make sense.

ideas.what: Support and co-support of a family of pieces defined via a disjointness relation: cosupp = orthogonal, supp = double orthogonal, with supports as closed elements Σ_M
ideas.modern_name: Birkhoff polarity / Galois connection closure; analogue of regular open sets
ideas.where_published: Unpublished 1986 Analysis situs notes; Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only announces 'tame topology' in general terms

ideas.what: Constructible (internal) support: supp° of a subfamily majorised by a figure
ideas.modern_name: Analogue of definable/constructible sets in a stratified or o-minimal setting
ideas.usually_credited_to: Constructible sets: Chevalley/EGA; tame topology: van den Dries et al.

ideas.what: 'Fully faithful' realisation functor X ↦ |X|: the complement of each figure is covered by open parts of pieces combinatorially disjoint from it, ensuring combinatorial supports match geometric ones
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility condition between a combinatorial stratification (face poset) and its geometric realisation; cf. a regular cell complex / frontier condition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather); the regular CW complex face-poset reconstruction is classical

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches an axiomatic, purely combinatorial 'analysis situs'. A category of pieces with a disjointness polarity defines supports, and a 'full faithfulness' axiom identifies them with geometric supports of a realisation. It is a candidate foundation for tame topology parallel to, but independent of, o-minimality; the thread is not visibly developed in the literature.
missed.quote: je vois à présent quelle est l'hypothèse générale qui assure une "bon comportement" pour des "supports (internes) constructibles"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is of historical interest as a concrete glimpse of how Grothendieck intended to realise the Esquisse's 'topologie modérée'. It is a combinatorial-lattice approach rather than a model-theoretic one. Mathematically the ingredients (polarities, face posets) are standard.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working page with an example and two definitions in an unpublished axiomatisation of tame topology. It documents Grothendieck's approach, but the mathematics (double-orthogonal closure, a covering condition on complements) is elementary and close to classical notions.
transcription_corrections: Page number at top reads '76', not '78' (consistent with previous 75 / next 77).
The relation is '|X|° ∪ |Y|° ⊂ φ(supp°({Y,X}))' (inclusion), not '∈'; the struck '{Y}' precedes it.
The inserted 'A' belongs to 'Un élément A de Σ_M', not to 'une A catégorie'.
The first line is likely 'C'est donc ici qu'on aura besoin de l'hypothèse plus haut, dans toute sa force.*'.
The functor target is probably 𝔓(P) (subsets of P), written 'M → 𝔓(P)'.
The functor phrase is roughly 'On dit qu'un foncteur support constructible(?) externe [fidèle] X ↦ |X|, M → 𝔓(P) est pleinement fidèle (pour F), si elle...'.
The margin note is mostly illegible; legible fragments include 'pour les puissances finies', '|Z| ∩ |X| = ∅', and '|Z| ⊂ p^{-1}(|X|)'.
